description: The bar chart illustrates the comparison of perplexity values for two pruning strategies—“Per-Output” (blue bars) and “Per-Layer” (orange bars)—across eight different sparsity rates (10% to 80%) in large language models, as presented in the paper “DLP: Dynamic Layerwise Pruning.” The vertical axis, labeled “Perplexity,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹ to 10³, with major gridlines at 10, 100, and 1000, to accommodate the wide range of values and highlight differences more clearly. The horizontal axis lists sparsity rates in 10% increments from 10% to 80%. At low sparsity rates (10%–50%), both strategies yield very similar and low perplexity values, with bars clustered near 10¹. As sparsity increases to 60%, perplexity begins to rise slightly for both, with “Per-Layer” showing a marginally higher value. At 70% sparsity, “Per-Output” reaches approximately 15 and “Per-Layer” approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, perplexity increases sharply: “Per-Output” reaches approximately 400, while “Per-Layer” exceeds 600, indicating significantly higher model degradation under high sparsity for the per-layer approach. The chart visually emphasizes that while both methods perform similarly at low sparsity, the per-layer pruning incurs a greater cost in perplexity at higher sparsity levels.
